    Lemma 4.9: weights on representation-finite posets #

    lem:poset-weights (scalar-normalization.tex): "If the incidence algebra of a finite poset R is representation-finite, every additive weight, with values in any abelian group, has the form w(x,y) = ζ_y − ζ_x."

    Proof of the source: "Remove a minimal element s and put U = {y : s < y}. Distinct connected components of U lie in distinct components of R ∖ {s}. Otherwise, put a one-dimensional space at every vertex, assign the map one to every comparison outside s, and assign maps λ ∈ k* from s to one component of U and one to the others. These are representations. An isomorphism must have the same scalar at all vertices of each component of R ∖ {s}. Two components of U in the same such component therefore force equality of the parameters. This produces infinitely many isomorphism classes of fixed dimension, contrary to finite representation type. […] By induction normalize all weights on R ∖ {s} to zero. The remaining weights from s are constant on each component of U. Adjust the object values separately on the corresponding components of R ∖ {s} to remove these constants."

    The representations are right modules over the incidence algebra on a convex connected set D (thinRep); the source restricts them to the component of s, where they are indecomposable. The removal of minimal elements runs through the up-sets of R, whose components are convex in R, so the representations of all steps are representations of the incidence algebra of R itself (no corner argument is needed).
